evals.prompt: We're Brightfold, API observability SaaS, about 6,200 people on our developer newsletter which goes out monthly. Open rate has slid from 38% in January to 29% last issue and our CMO wants us to go weekly to stay top of mind. Last quarter we shipped 4 releases, 2 blog posts and ran 1 webinar. Tomasz on devrel writes it, he can give about 3 hours per issue; nobody else has touched it. Can you put together the plan for moving to weekly?
evals.expected_output: A direct no to weekly, then a charter: supply counted at roughly 2-3 time-bound items a month, cadence derived from that rate and the 3 hours per issue (monthly holds), opens demoted to directional, demand marked unproven pending click data, the missing backup named as an open gate condition, curated ecosystem and personal letter deleted, own-surface digest kept monthly with the slow-down/speed-up rule.
expectations: Opens with a direct answer to the weekly question, declining the move to weekly, before any charter section
States that cadence is never raised to fix engagement
Counts supply by source from the figures given, 4 releases, 2 posts and 1 webinar over three months, as roughly 2-3 time-bound items per month
Shows that the counted rate cannot fill a weekly issue and derives the supported cadence from that rate and the 3 hours per issue, keeping monthly or slower
Treats the open-rate slide from 38% to 29% as directional rather than a target, citing mail-privacy open inflation
Asks for clicks per delivered email, unique clickers, unsubscribes, complaints and replies for the last six issues before judging reader demand
Marks the gate's demand condition unproven for lack of click data, with a pre-agreed threshold for the next issue, rather than passing or failing it
Flags that no backup is named and treats the missing backup as an unmet gate condition, carried as a named open question rather than an invented name
Deletes the curated ecosystem and personal-letter shapes because no backup exists, and says which shapes were deleted
Recommends the own-surface digest at monthly cadence as the shape
Does not propose subject-line tests, emojis, or resends to non-openers as the response to falling opens
States the slow-down and speed-up rule: slow after two consecutive thin issues, speed up only after three consecutive full ones

evals.prompt: Kelvane makes a payments SDK. Dario wrote our biweekly developer newsletter for two years and left in July; the last issue went out 11 weeks ago. The list is 14,000: about 9,000 came from the newsletter checkbox on our site, the other 5,000 we imported from product signups in 2024 (roughly a third EU, a third UK, a third US, mostly personal gmail-type addresses; the signup form had no unsubscribe or opt-out option). The sending tool is on Dario's personal login and his credit card, and the sending subdomain DNS was set up under his account too. Numbers before the pause: 44% opens, 1.1% clicks, a few replies per issue. What we shipped in the last three months: 6 releases, 3 blog posts, 3 community call recordings; community members also posted about 15 useful forum answers. Our head of marketing wants to relaunch next week with a full redesign and a big 'we're back' issue, targeting 50% opens. Plan the relaunch.
evals.expected_output: A rescue charter that starts from the list's numbers and consent, not the redesign: consent classified segment by segment (EU/UK imported individuals suppressed and invited once in-product, US imported kept on opt-out), gate metrics computed on the lawful segment, accounts and domain moved to the organisation before any send, supply counted with forum answers as external, monthly cadence derived and biweekly rejected, 50% opens rejected as a target, restart issue stating cadence, author and unsubscribe, backup and reviewer required.
expectations: Begins with the existing list's numbers and consent provenance, not with the redesign or the 'we're back' issue
Classifies consent before computing gate metrics, splitting the 9,000 checkbox signups from the 5,000 imported product accounts
States that the EU and UK individual addresses in the imported segment have no lawful basis, because no opt-out was offered at signup so the soft opt-in does not apply
Keeps the US imported addresses mailable on a working opt-out, honest headers and a postal address
Suppresses only the no-basis segment and invites it once through the product, never by email
Computes the gate's demand condition on the lawful segment, not on the whole 14,000
Requires the sending account, list export, sending subdomain and archive to move from Dario's personal login and card to an organisation account before the restart
Counts the 15 forum answers as external supply because community members wrote them, even on the company's own forum
Derives a monthly cadence from about 4 time-bound items per month (6 releases, 3 posts, 3 recordings per quarter) and rejects biweekly on supply
Rejects 50% opens as a target and reports opens as directional
Specifies that the restart issue states what changed: the new cadence, who writes it now, and how to unsubscribe
Does not let the next-week date skip the account transfer or the consent classification
Names a backup and a reviewer as gate conditions, marking the owner condition blocked with the missing name, its owner and a dated re-check if none is supplied
Does not design the redesign, header or visual refresh

evals.prompt: Orrin Labs here, three of us (me plus two engineers) building ferrule, an open-source CLI with a hosted tier. We ship roughly two releases a month, no blog, releases go on the GitHub releases page and that's it. Every advisor says we need a newsletter. I was thinking 'Ferrule Friday', a short weekly email. I can spare maybe an hour a month on comms in total. Should we do it, and if so set it up.
evals.expected_output: A direct answer: no email newsletter now, feed first. The five shapes ranked in efficiency order with the ranking said aloud, three shapes deleted on the one-hour ceiling, feed only recommended, the missing public changelog with RSS/Atom named as the prerequisite routed to changelog-writing, weekly rejected on supply, advisor opinion rejected as demand evidence, and the condition for adding email later stated.
expectations: Opens with a direct answer to 'should we do it': not an email newsletter now, feed first
Presents the five shapes in efficiency order, feed only, own-surface digest, curated ecosystem, community-edited, personal letter, and states the ranking explicitly
Deletes the curated ecosystem, community-edited and personal-letter shapes on the one-hour-a-month effort ceiling, and names the deletions
Recommends feed only as the shape
States that feed only needs a public changelog with an RSS or Atom feed, which the project lacks, so building it comes first
Routes the changelog build to samber/developer-relations-skills@changelog-writing
Rejects weekly 'Ferrule Friday' on the counted supply of about two releases a month and no blog
Treats advisors saying 'you need a newsletter' as not evidence of reader demand, and names explicit reader requests or users who never see the changelog as the evidence that would count
States the condition under which an editor and email get added later: the demand condition holding with evidence
Does not propose a signup form, list-growth tactics, or sending-platform selection
Writes the gate result naming which condition failed or is unproven, rather than a blanket 'not now'

evals.prompt: Tessamere, dev tooling. We have a newsletter list of 3,100 that hasn't been sent to in 8 months since Ruth left. Our marketing lead says nobody reads it, last issue got 12% opens, and wants to delete the list and move on, we've got a 2k-member Discord and a public changelog with RSS now anyway. For what it's worth the clicks on the last six issues were 0.9%, 1.1%, 0.8%, 1.0%, 0.7%, 0.9% and each issue got 2 to 5 replies. Can we just kill it?
evals.expected_output: Stop mode run through the gate and the sunset table: the silent-over-six-months trigger fires a re-permission issue before anything else, the 12% opens are set aside, the click series reads flat against its own trend with the ~1% median as context only, replies count as demand, the owner condition is the one that fails, and closure (or feed-only downgrade) happens through a final issue pointing to the Discord and feed, never by silently deleting the list.
expectations: Runs the gate and the sunset table before answering, rather than accepting deletion on the marketing lead's say-so
Fires the list-silent-more-than-six-months trigger and prescribes a re-permission issue first, suppressing non-responders
Does not use the 12% open rate as evidence that nobody reads it
Reads the 0.7-1.1% click series against the list's own trend as flat rather than falling
Presents the roughly 1% software-sender median click rate as context, never as a target
Counts the 2-5 replies per issue as demand evidence
Names the owner condition as the gate condition that fails, since no owner or backup exists
Treats the Discord and the changelog feed under the 'need moved' trigger and prescribes closing with a final issue that points readers to the replacement
States that a downgrade to feed only means one final issue pointing at the feed, then no further sends
Does not recommend deleting the list without a final issue
States who holds the sending account, list export and archive after closure, assigning them to the organisation

evals.prompt: Halvorsen Data, we make a vector database. Our monthly developer digest is doing fine, 8,000 subscribers, written by Ines. We now want to add external links from the ecosystem and sell one slot per issue to integration partners, first one is ready to pay for the top slot. Two questions from our PM: what's the industry standard ratio of our own content to external links, and can the paying partner take the lead slot? Constraints from legal: never name customers, no comparisons with competitors. Also product wants to tease an unannounced feature in next issue. Write our curation rule.
evals.expected_output: A curation-rule section: no published industry ratio exists, so the share is a number the team chooses and is labelled a house rule; written inclusion criteria and an exclusion list carrying named customers, competitor comparisons and the unannounced feature; sponsored placements labelled, held to the same inclusion criteria, capped per issue, with payment alone not deciding the lead slot; gated links excluded; the three-trial-digests path to the curated ecosystem shape.
expectations: States that no published industry own-versus-external ratio exists and declines to cite one
Sets the own-versus-external share as a number the team chooses and labels it a house rule
Writes inclusion criteria in words plus an exclusion list
Carries named customers, competitor comparisons and the unannounced feature into the exclusion list
Requires every paid or partner placement to carry a 'sponsored' label
Requires sponsored items to meet the same inclusion criteria as editorial items
Sets a per-issue cap on sponsored placements
Does not let payment alone decide the lead slot; the partner item takes any slot only if it meets the inclusion criteria
Prescribes three monthly digests each carrying one trial external section whose items drew clicks before moving to the curated ecosystem shape
Excludes gated content and links that capture email addresses from external items
Does not write issue copy, the sponsor pitch, or the media kit

evals.prompt: Lindqvist Systems, IoT device management. Our fortnightly developer newsletter exists to keep current customers using the features we ship. VP of marketing wants a dashboard with targets: 45% open rate, 8% click-to-open, and 'reach'. Two things I noticed: click rate jumped from 1.3% to about 6% over the last two issues, right after we onboarded three enterprise customers whose staff all use corporate mail gateways; and unsubscribes went from about 0.1% to 0.25% over the past year. Build the measurement section of our newsletter plan.
evals.expected_output: A measurement section with no open-derived primary metric: clicks per delivered email, unique clickers across the last N issues, unsubscribes and complaints, replies as primaries; feature adoption from newsletter links as the retention outcome signal; the 6% click jump attributed to gateway machine clicks and filtered with a named method that is reported; the unsubscribe rise explained by one-click unsubscribe under the 2024 bulk-sender rules; quarterly review against the list's own trend with house-rule thresholds.
expectations: Makes no open-derived metric (open rate, click-to-open, open-based reach) a primary metric or target
Reports opens and click-to-open as directional only
Sets clicks per delivered email, unique clickers across the last N issues, unsubscribes and complaints, and replies as the primary signals
Picks feature adoption from newsletter links as the outcome signal, matching the retention funding reason
Does not pick signups from non-users or submissions per issue as the outcome signal
Attributes the jump from 1.3% to 6% clicks to corporate mail gateways following links on arrival, and excludes those machine clicks
Names a concrete filter: the platform's bot-click filter, or discarding clicks within seconds of delivery and sends where every link was clicked
Requires the report to state which bot-click filter was used
Explains the rise from 0.1% to 0.25% unsubscribes as consistent with one-click unsubscribe under the 2024 bulk-sender rules, so not alone a content signal
Sets a quarterly review against the list's own trend rather than against platform benchmarks
Labels every threshold set as a house rule
Replaces 'reach' with unique clickers across the last N issues rather than an open-based multi-issue reach figure

evals.prompt: I maintain Larkspur, an open-source Kubernetes operator, about 40 regular contributors. We run a triage meeting every Tuesday and contributors already post a 'what we merged this week' thread in GitHub Discussions. I want a newsletter as a compounding asset for the project, no deadline. I can put in about 3 hours per issue. Nobody has agreed to be backup yet, I'll find someone eventually. Which kind of newsletter should we run and how do we set it up?
evals.expected_output: Community-edited promoted on its two stated conditions (contributors already submit, weekly governance cycle), curated ecosystem and personal letter deleted on the missing backup with the compounding mandate unable to revive them, the owner-and-backup gate condition marked blocked with the missing fact, its owner and a dated re-check, cadence anchored to the Tuesday triage, sections mirroring the cycle with section editors, intake by pull request or form, Discussions items counted as external, submissions per issue as the outcome signal, feed-only fallback.
expectations: Promotes the community-edited shape on the two stated conditions: contributors already submit content, and a weekly governance cycle exists
Deletes the curated ecosystem and personal-letter shapes because no backup exists, and says so
States that the compounding mandate does not revive a shape the backup answer deleted
Marks the owner-and-backup gate condition blocked, names the missing backup as the fact, assigns it to the maintainer, and sets a dated re-check
Does not invent or assume a backup
Anchors the cadence to the Tuesday triage cycle
Mirrors the section template on the governance cycle and names section editors as the ownership model
Specifies submissions by pull request or form as the intake
Counts the Discussions thread items as external supply because community members wrote them
Picks submissions per issue as the outcome signal for the contributor-view funding reason
Keeps a feed-only fallback if no backup exists by the re-check date

evals.prompt: Marrowgate, CI platform. We've had a monthly developer newsletter for a year and want to formalise it. Current state: owned by 'the devrel team', nine sections, when nothing shipped we fill it with generic tips, and we tack billing and security notices on at the end so we don't need a separate send. The sending domain is registered on an ex-contractor's registrar account. There's no archive, we just send and forget. Write the template and the ownership section.
evals.expected_output: A five-to-seven-section template table with source, owner, item range and empty-section rule per row, filler replaced by drop-or-evergreen rules; ownership naming a person, a backup and a reviewer with hours, the domain and every account moved to the organisation, billing and security notices pulled out into their own transactional stream, a public-URL and archive decision, the running cost and its budget line, the runbook location and a handoff checklist.
expectations: Cuts the template to five to seven sections in a fixed order
Gives every section a source, an owner, an item range and an empty-section rule
Replaces filler with either dropping the empty section or a named evergreen slot
Rejects 'the devrel team' as an owner and requires a named owner, a named backup and a reviewer, each with hours per issue
Moves the sending domain from the ex-contractor's registrar account to the organisation
Removes billing and security notices from the newsletter, keeping it a separate consented stream from transactional email
Cites that a message mixing commercial and transactional content counts as commercial when the transactional part does not come first or the subject line reads as commercial
Decides whether each issue gets a public URL and names where the archive lives
Names the running cost and the budget line that pays it
Names where the runbook lives and includes a handoff checklist
Produces the template as a table with the columns Section, Source, Owner, Items, When empty

evals.prompt: Veldt, GraphQL gateway startup. Quick one: curated ecosystem newsletter or a plain product digest? Just pick one for us, we'll handle the rest.
evals.expected_output: No pick. One interview question at a time, multiple-choice, starting with mode, then supply counts for the last three months, then owner hours and backup, plus the date, compounding and effort-ceiling questions, with the reason stated: a shape chosen before supply and owner hours are known is a guess the team will miss.
expectations: Does not pick a shape before the mode, the last-three-months supply counts and the owner hours are known
Asks one question per message
Offers multiple-choice answers where possible
Asks for counts of what shipped in the last three months, not adjectives
Asks who owns it, hours per issue, who backs up, who reviews, and who holds the sending account, list export and domain
Asks for the landing date, whether it is a one-off win or a compounding asset, and the effort ceiling in hours per month
States why it will not pick yet: a cadence chosen before supply and owner hours are known is a guess the team will miss
Offers to carry any partial answer as a named open question rather than refusing to proceed
Stores interview answers in devrel-context.md when file-based memory is in use, or in the harness memory otherwise
